mainTopic: Selling a house: which attached structures are not included, what a יציע is, and the four-אמות minimum
overview: The משנה teaches that when someone sells a house without spelling out what is included, some attached areas stay with the seller: the יציע, the inner room, and a roof that has a ten-טפחים railing. רבי יהודה adds that a roof with a צורת פתח is also not sold. The גמרא asks what a יציע is. One view says it is an attic (אפתא), and רב יוסף says it is a windowed side structure (בדקא חלילה). The גמרא then shows how these two definitions lead to different results. רב יוסף also teaches that this kind of structure has three names, יציע, צלע and תא, and brings a source for each. מר זוטרא limits the משנה: a יציע is held back from the sale only if it is at least four אמות. רבינא challenges him from the בור and דות, which are held back at any size, and מר זוטרא answers that a pit has a different use from the house, while a יציע has the same use. Finally, the גמרא asks why the משנה needs to mention the inner room at all, since a יציע is already not sold. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Selling a house does not include the gallery, the inner room, or a fenced roof
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a plain sale of a house does not include the יציע, the inner room, or a roof with a ten-טפחים railing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sells a house, he has not sold the יציע, even if it opens into the house. He also has not sold the room inside it, or the roof, if the roof has a railing ten טפחים high.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists parts attached to a house that are NOT included when the house is sold without details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sale only covers what people normally mean by 'the house.' The יציע and the inner room count as separate rooms, even though you reach them through the house. A roof with a tall railing is a usable area of its own, so it is not included either.

keyTerms.meaning: A gallery or side structure attached to a house
A railing or parapet around a roof

steps.confusionAlert: Even if the יציע opens right into the house, it is still not sold. Being connected does not make it part of the house.

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הַבַּיִת – לֹא מָכַר יָצִיעַ,
phrases.english: One who sells the house has not sold the gallery,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא פְּתוּחָה לְתוֹכוֹ;
phrases.english: even though it opens into it;
nor the room that is inside it;
nor the roof,

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מַעֲקֶה גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים.
phrases.english: when it has a railing ten handbreadths high.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הַבַּיִת – לֹא מָכַר יָצִיעַ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plain sale of a house excludes the יציע (even if it opens inward), the inner room, and a roof with a ten-טפחים railing.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a doorway-shaped frame also keeps the roof out of the sale
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a roof with a צורת פתח is not sold, even if its railing is less than ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if the roof has the shape of a doorway, it is not sold, even if it is not ten טפחים high.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds another way a roof can be counted as separate from the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion needs a ten-טפחים railing to mark the roof as its own area. רבי יהודה says a doorway frame (two posts with a beam across the top) also marks it as separate, even without that height.

keyTerms.meaning: The form of a doorway: two upright posts with a beam across the top

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If it has the form of a doorway,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים – אֵינוֹ מָכוּר.
phrases.english: even though it is not ten handbreadths high, it is not sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ צוּרַת פֶּתַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second way for the roof to be excluded, beyond the ten-טפחים railing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צורת פתח on the roof keeps it out of the sale, even without a ten-טפחים railing.

steps.title: What is a יציע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the word יציע in the משנה means.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of an unclear word in the משנה. This sets up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before we can know what stays with the seller, we have to know exactly which structure the משנה is talking about. This is a question to clarify a term, not a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows and explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is a 'gallery'?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact definition of the יציע mentioned in the משנה.

steps.title: Two definitions: an attic or a windowed side structure
steps.stepSummary: In Babylonia they said יציע means אפתא (an attic); רב יוסף said it means בדקא חלילה (a windowed side structure).
steps.simpleTranslation: Here they explained it as an attic. רב יוסף said: it is a windowed side structure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different answers to the question of what a יציע is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view says the יציע is an attic, a space built on top of the house. רב יוסף says it is a structure with windows, built next to the house. Each definition changes which structure the משנה leaves out of the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: A windowed structure attached to a building

phrases.english: Here they explained it as: an attic.
Rav Yosef said: a windowed structure.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יציע is either an attic (אפתא) or a windowed side structure (בדקא חלילה, the view of רב יוסף).

steps.title: The practical difference between the two definitions
steps.stepSummary: If even an attic is not sold, then a windowed structure is surely not sold. But if the יציע is only the windowed structure, an attic would be sold with the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says an attic is not sold, then all the more so a windowed structure is not sold. According to the one who says it is a windowed structure, an attic is sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the two definitions lead to different results in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An attic is more tied to the house than a windowed side structure. So if the משנה leaves out even the attic, it surely leaves out the more separate windowed structure. But if the משנה only meant the windowed structure, then the more connected attic goes along with the house.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

steps.whatToRemember: The attic view is the broader one: it leaves both the attic and the windowed structure out of the sale. רב יוסף's view leaves out only the windowed structure, so the attic is sold with the house.

phrases.english: According to the one who says an attic is not sold,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן בַּדְקָא חֲלִילָה לָא מִזְדַּבְּנָא;
phrases.english: all the more so a windowed structure is not sold;
according to the one who says it is a windowed structure,
but an attic is sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the practical result of the two definitions in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The attic view leaves out both structures. The windowed-structure view leaves out only that one, so the attic is sold.

steps.title: רב יוסף: three names for an attached structure, each with a verse
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that this kind of structure is called יציע, צלע, and תא, and brings a פסוק for each name.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: it has three names: יציע, צלע, and תא. יציע, as it says: 'The lowest יציע was five אמות wide.' צלע, as it says: 'And the side chambers, chamber over chamber, thirty-three times.' תא, as it says: 'And the cell was one reed long and one reed wide, and between the cells five אמות.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף shows that the תנ"ך uses three different words for the same kind of attached side structure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name is backed by a פסוק describing side structures of the בית המקדש. This teaches that יציע, צלע and תא all mean the same thing: a small structure attached to a main building.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
It has three names:
gallery, side chamber, cell.
'Gallery,' as it is written:
'The lowest gallery was five cubits wide.'
'Side chamber,' as it is written:
'And the side chambers, chamber over chamber,'
'thirty-three times.'
'Cell,' as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהַתָּא קָנֶה אֶחָד אֹרֶךְ וְקָנֶה אֶחָד רֹחַב,
phrases.english: 'And the cell was one reed long and one reed wide,'
'and between the cells five cubits.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּאנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף: שָׁלֹשׁ שֵׁמוֹת יֵשׁ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues defining יציע by showing its other names in פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יציע, צלע and תא are three names for the same kind of attached structure, each found in a פסוק.

steps.title: Another source for the name תא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a different source for the name תא: the measurements of the היכל wall and the cell behind it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it from here: 'The wall of the היכל was six, and the cell was six, and the wall of the cell was five.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second source showing that a side structure is called תא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This source lists the wall of the היכל, then the תא next to it, then the wall of the תא. It clearly shows a תא as a chamber attached to the side of a main building.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary building of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And if you want, say it from here:
'The wall of the Sanctuary was six,'
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה in מסכת מדות 4:7, not from a פסוק. The numbers are in אמות.

phrases.english: 'and the cell was six, the wall of the cell was five.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another source for the name תא, in place of the פסוק in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That a side structure is called תא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה מדות 4:7, describing the היכל wall, the תא, and the wall of the תא.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: the יציע is excluded only if it is four אמות
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא limits the משנה: a יציע stays with the seller only if it measures at least four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: this is only when it is four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא goes back to the משנה's rule and adds a size condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A structure that is at least four by four אמות is big enough to count as a room of its own, so it is not part of the house sale. If it is smaller, it is treated as part of the house and is sold with it.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is only when it is

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה leaves the יציע out of the sale only if it is at least four by four אמות. A smaller one goes along with the house.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
And that is only when it is four cubits.
phrases.notes: He means four by four אמות. 'That' refers back to the משנה's rule that the gallery is not sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: וְהוּא דְּהָוֵי אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's rule about the יציע and limits it by size.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יציע is excluded from the sale only if it is at least four by four אמות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a practical size threshold that decides whether an attached structure goes with the house or stays with the seller.

steps.title: רבינא asks: does a pit also need four אמות?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges מר זוטרא: if a יציע must be four אמות to be held back from the sale, then a בור and דות should also need four אמות. But the משנה holds them back with no size limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to מר זוטרא: You say a יציע is held back only if it is four אמות. Then what about the pit? The משנה says the seller does not sell the בור or the דות, even if he wrote 'depth and height' in the deed. Would you also say they are held back only if they are four אמות, and otherwise not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks מר זוטרא's four-אמות rule by applying it to a similar case, the pit and cistern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה on 64a holds back the בור and דות from the sale with no mention of size. If a minimum size were needed for a יציע, it should seem needed there too. A pit is usually smaller than four אמות, so then it would almost never be held back.

keyTerms.meaning: According to you, by your own view
If so, then... (introduces a challenge from what follows)
A pit or cistern dug into the ground
A cistern, usually a built-up one
Depth and height (wording in a deed of sale)

phrases.english: Ravina said to Mar Zutra:
According to you, who say
it is held back only if it is four cubits;
phrases.notes: This is his rule from Step 8 about the יציע.

phrases.english: if so, then
regarding a pit, as we learned in a Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַבּוֹר וְלֹא אֶת הַדּוּת –
phrases.english: he has sold neither the pit nor the cistern,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתַב לוֹ עוּמְקָא וְרוּמָא;
phrases.english: even if he wrote for him 'depth and height';

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי אִי הָווּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת – אִין,
phrases.english: so too, if they are four cubits, yes, they are held back,
and if not, no?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִידָךְ דְּאָמְרַתְּ עַד דְּהָוֵי אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת; אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the four-אמות limit that מר זוטרא set in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's rule that a יציע is held back only at four אמות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Applying the same size rule to a בור and דות would contradict the משנה, which holds them back with no size condition

steps.title: A pit has a different use; a gallery has the same use as the house
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא answers that the cases are not alike. A pit is used differently from a house, so it is always separate. A יציע is used like the house, so it counts as separate only if it is four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, the pit has its own use and the house has its own use. Here, the יציע and the house have the same use. So if the יציע is four אמות, it counts as its own space. If not, it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא defends his rule by showing why a pit is different from a יציע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What makes something separate from the house is having its own kind of use. A pit holds water, which is clearly different from living space, so it is separate at any size. A יציע is living space just like the house, so only a real size of four אמות makes it its own unit.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejecting a comparison)
This one and that one, both

steps.whatToRemember: A space is held back from a house sale when it is its own unit. A pit counts at any size because of its different use. A יציע, used like the house, counts only at four אמות.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, this one has its own separate use,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the pit, which holds water, and 'that one' in the next line is the house, used for living.

phrases.english: and that one has its own separate use;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא – אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי חֲדָא תַּשְׁמִישְׁתָּא הִיא;
phrases.english: here, both this and that have one use;
if it is four cubits, it is significant,
and if not, it is not significant.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (different use vs. same use)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A pit and a יציע should follow the same size rule
steps.terutzMaskana: A space with a different use is always separate. A space with the same use as the house is separate only at four אמות.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to mention the inner room?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה, the inner room, and asks why it is needed. If even a יציע is not sold, a room behind the house is surely not sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'nor the room behind it.' The גמרא asks: Now that a יציע is not sold, do we even need to be told that a room is not sold?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the משנה and asks why they are needed. It is setting up an answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יציע is attached to the house, yet it is still held back. A separate inner room seems even more clearly its own unit, so it should be obvious that it is held back. The question is why the משנה bothers to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: That is further inside, behind it
Is it necessary (to say)? Meaning it should be obvious

steps.confusionAlert: The first line is not the גמרא speaking. It is a quote from the משנה, and the question comes right after it.

phrases.english: 'Nor the room that is inside it.'
Now, if a gallery is not sold,
is it necessary to say a room is not?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא יָצִיעַ לָא מִיזְדַּבַּן, חֶדֶר מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the יציע discussion to the next clause of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause about the inner room
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The clause seems unnecessary, since it follows clearly from the rule that a יציע is not sold
